Scalar features per query — no span claims. Five router signals; each scalar answers one question the Strategy Router cares about.
Scalars: length_words (regex \w+ count) · length_chars. Very short queries give dense too little context → sparse-safe. Long queries carry enough signal for dense. REGEX engine — no model required.

Example: stopword_ratio=0.50 ("the best restaurants in Berlin") · 0.0 ("restaurant Berlin cheap")
Why?: Scalars: stopword_ratio · stopword_count. REGEX fallback of natural_language_share — closed stopword list, no spaCy required. High = natural phrasing → dense; near-zero = keyword telegram → sparse.

Scalar: natural_language_share — fraction of tokens that are UD closed-class POS (ADP/AUX/CCONJ/DET/NUM/PART/PRON/SCONJ). Near 0 = keyword telegram → sparse; 0.4–0.5 = natural sentence → dense. Requires pinned spaCy model (en_core_web_sm).

Example: word_variation_share=0.25 ("running dogs were found") · 0.0 ("run dog find")
Why?: Scalar: word_variation_share — fraction of alpha tokens whose lemma ≠ surface form (running → run). Grammar-caused vocabulary mismatch risk: high → embeddings help; zero → BM25 safe. Requires pinned spaCy model.

Example: nesting_depth=4 · statement_count=2 ("the paper that introduced attention, which was later adopted in GPT")
Why?: Scalars: nesting_depth (max dependency-tree depth) · statement_count (clausal dep count). Deep / multi-statement → dense or decompose+rerank. Read jointly with natural_language_share — parser hallucinates structure on non-sentences. Requires pinned spaCy model.

Scalar: widest_list_size — how many equal parts does the longest and/or/comma chain string together? Wide-but-flat enumeration nesting_depth cannot see. Read jointly with natural_language_share. Requires pinned spaCy model.
